reserveReview.rationale: At Ethereum block 26197000 (2026-10-15T09:24:59Z; hash 0x7f8f6377ac8f3948e1ac61d81c1a236b58c7ef57ef2743f18189cca1127aa66d), asset() is USDC, totalSupply()=9981619073650174219359686 raw 18-decimal shares and totalAssets()=10183216864889 raw 6-decimal USDC. adaptersLength()=1 and adapters(0)=0x7df529c92b5744b13be10f06e0c0846186a24f79. Its four market IDs reconcile expectedSupplyAssets to realAssets()=10183216864889; idle USDC=0. Lender-claim allocations are WBTC 71.29467103%, cbBTC 26.23508602%, weETH 2.47024295% and wstETH 2 atomic USDC units. These are USDC lender-claim weights by borrower collateral, not holdings of the collateral tokens. All four adapter positions have zero borrow shares and zero posted collateral; immutable market LLTV is 86%. The 100% reserve row covers the entire USDC-denominated lending-and-idle envelope. It does not imply cash backing, ownership of pledged collateral or independent financial reconciliation. Immediate vault and adapter custody is on-chain. About 97.53% of the lender claims are against custodial WBTC/cbBTC collateral, so whole-book custody is mixed. Coinbase identifies itself as cbBTC backing custodian; WBTC discloses custodial BTC reserves without allocating this vault to named reserve custodians. No custody-provider share, legal segregation, insolvency priority, independent vault financial assurance or guaranteed stressed realization is inferred.
